Investigational CNS-directed AAV delivery of HEXA and HEXB aims to restore HexA. Expanded access treated two infants in 2022; a subsequent nonrandomized dose-escalation trial treated seven Tay-Sachs and two Sandhoff patients. CSF enzyme activity increased, peaking near 12 weeks before declining, with partial or temporary infantile clinical stabilization. Two of three juvenile participants developed new or worsening dystonia and juvenile enrollment stopped. Vector-associated immune/transaminase responses required corticosteroids. Clinical efficacy remains incomplete and uncontrolled; serum Hex activity is not a CNS surrogate. TSHA-101 uses a different bicistronic AAV9 product from the dual AAVrh8 vectors in these publications.

nodes.description: Progressive motor pathway dysfunction produces spasticity, particularly in juvenile disease; this is distinct from an unspecified spasm.

evidence.reference_title: HEXA Disorders.
evidence.snippet: Spasticity, dysphagia, and seizures are present by the end of the first decade of life, with death within the second decade of life, usually by aspiration.

evidence.reference_title: HEXA Disorders.
evidence.snippet: Late-onset TSD presents in older teens or young adults with a slowly progressive spectrum of neurologic symptoms including lower-extremity weakness with muscle atrophy, dysarthria, incoordination, tremor, mild spasticity and/or dystonia, and psychiatric manifestations including acute psychosis.

nodes.description: Action tremor may occur in late-onset disease; co-occurring myoclonus is represented separately.

evidence.reference_title: Late-onset Tay-Sachs disease.
evidence.snippet: irregular action tremor and stimulus-sensitive myoclonus of the arms
